record.original_question: Find exact formulas for the two fundamental extremal functions for Golomb rulers: the minimum possible length n of a Golomb ruler with a given number m of points, and the maximum possible number of points m in a Golomb ruler of a given length n.

evidence.quote: The two fundamental problems in the field are to determine a) the maximal possible m for a fixed n, and b) the minimal possible n for a fixed m.
Problem 25. Provide exact formulas for the length of optimally short Golomb rulers of a given number of points, and for the number of points of optimally dense Golomb rulers of a given length.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Golomb ruler is a finite set of nonnegative integers $\{a_0 < a_1 < \dots < a_{m-1}\}$ such that all pairwise differences $a_j - a_i$ (for $0 \le i < j \le m-1$) are distinct. The number of points of the ruler is $m$, and its length is $a_{m-1} - a_0$ (equivalently, one may assume $a_0 = 0$ and the length is $a_{m-1}$). Define the two extremal functions:

- $G(m)$ = the minimum possible length of a Golomb ruler with exactly $m$ points;
- $M(n)$ = the maximum possible number of points of a Golomb ruler of length $n$.

Provide an exact closed-form formula for $G(m)$ as a function of the integer $m \ge 1$, and an exact closed-form formula for $M(n)$ as a function of the integer $n \ge 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: No closed-form exact formula is known for either the minimum length of an optimal Golomb ruler with m points or the maximum number of points of a Golomb ruler of length n. Optimal lengths have been verified computationally only up to 28 marks (as of distributed search results through 2023), and research has focused on asymptotic bounds and constructions (e.g., Singer, Bose–Chowla) producing near-optimal rulers. The problem of giving exact formulas remains open.

status_evidence.title: Golomb ruler - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Although the lengths of the optimal n-mark Golomb rulers are not known for n > 28... no known formula for G(n).
status_evidence.claim: No closed-form formula is known; optimality verified only up to 28 marks.

status_evidence.title: A003022 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: Length of shortest (or optimal) Golomb ruler with n marks.
status_evidence.claim: OEIS lists known values but no closed formula for the sequence.

status_evidence.title: Golomb Ruler -- MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Construction methods give near-optimal rulers; no exact formula is known.
status_evidence.claim: Only constructions and bounds are known, not exact formulas.
